assumptions.choice: used bt.indicators.PercentChange(close, period=N) for the (Close/Close[-N]-1) calc instead of manual close[-N] indexing
assumptions.reason: keeps warm-up handled by backtrader's automatic minperiod (canonical default), avoiding manual bar-skip guards while computing the exact same ratio the spec states.

assumptions.choice: entry leg of buy_bracket submitted as bt.Order.Market
assumptions.reason: spec doesn't state an entry order type; a market entry is the closest literal reading of 'open a long position' immediately on signal, and is the natural pairing with bracket TP/SL legs (stop/limit exectypes left at their bracket defaults).

assumptions.choice: size (shares) = position_usdt / data.close[0] at the signal bar
assumptions.reason: spec requires a fixed USDT-equivalent position size; the signal bar's close is the only price known at order-submission time, so it is used as the sizing reference.

assumptions.choice: TP (+tp_pct) and SL (-sl_pct) absolute prices passed to buy_bracket are computed from the signal bar's close rather than the market order's actual fill price
assumptions.reason: backtrader submits all three bracket legs atomically before the main order fills, and the main order (market) executes on the next bar's open under this harness's default fill timing, so the true fill price is unknown at the moment bracket prices must be fixed. The signal close is used as the closest literal entry-price proxy.

assumptions.choice: mode parameter is exposed but has no functional effect on backtest behavior
assumptions.reason: the spec's test/real mode switching refers to live-vs-paper broker connectivity, which does not exist in this fixed single-feed, harness-controlled backtest environment; only a placeholder parameter can be provided.
